correctness.rationale: The proof reduces restrained domination to an isolate-free condition on the two clique complements after first proving that the dominating set must meet both cliques. The singleton exceptions are then exhaustive because the only cross-clique edge is the bridge. The complement generating function partitions all valid cases disjointly into regular complements, the double bridge singleton, and the two oriented single-bridge cases. Algebraic conversion gives the stated polynomial. The minimum layer and total count follow directly. The standalone verifier independently checks the definition, structural criterion, and every coefficient for orders corresponding to parameters three through eight; this finite check is supporting evidence only, not the proof.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete cardinality distribution for a standard graph family, not just the minimum restrained-domination number. More structurally, it isolates the exact polynomial correction produced by a single bridge: the bridge is invisible to the ordinary domination polynomial but creates additional restrained dominating sets by rescuing singleton complement vertices. That contrast is a natural and reusable test case for how complement-side constraints react to graph surgery.
